title: Introduce a real runtime sandbox boundary
summary: Design and implement the first production-grade isolation backend for untrusted local agents, starting with Linux gVisor and preserving macOS subprocess mode as explicitly trusted-local only.
expectedFailureModes: The project claims sandbox-grade isolation while macOS and fallback subprocess mode still run trusted-local processes.
A sandbox-required agent silently falls back to subprocess execution when the configured Linux backend is unavailable.
The first sandbox backend leaks host filesystem, network, or environment access through permissive defaults.
The backend choice optimizes developer convenience but cannot support hostile third-party agent execution.
humanEscalation: Hardware and OS target selection for sandbox validation
Approval before claiming sandbox-grade isolation publicly
nextAction: Implement the manifest and runtime abstraction for trusted-local, linux-gvisor, and fail-closed sandbox-required modes.
